PARIS TRAVEL GUIDE — April 2026

TOP ATTRACTIONS
- Eiffel Tower: Book timed entry tickets online in advance (sells out weeks ahead)
- Louvre Museum: Allow 3-4 hours; closed Tuesdays; skip-the-line tickets recommended
- Musee d'Orsay: Impressionist collection, less crowded than the Louvre
- Notre-Dame Cathedral: Reconstruction ongoing through 2026; exterior viewing only
- Sainte-Chapelle: Stunning Gothic stained glass, easy to combine with Louvre

NEIGHBORHOODS
- Le Marais (3rd/4th): Historic district, Jewish quarter, great cafes and galleries
- Montmartre (18th): Sacre-Coeur, artist studios, best panoramic city views
- Saint-Germain-des-Pres (6th): Upscale shopping, classic Parisian brasseries
- Canal Saint-Martin (10th): Hip area, boutiques, trendy restaurants

PRACTICAL TIPS
- Metro: Navigo weekly pass ~¥220, covers all zones including CDG airport
- Currency: EUR; 1 EUR ~ 7.8 CNY as of April 2026
- Weather: 8-17 degrees C in late April; bring a light jacket and layers
- Tipping: Not mandatory, rounding up the bill is appreciated
- Language: Basic French phrases (bonjour, merci, s'il vous plait) go a long way

FOOD & DINING
- Breakfast: Croissant + cafe creme at a local boulangerie (under ¥40)
- Lunch: Croque monsieur or salade nicoise at a brasserie
- Dinner: Book ahead for popular restaurants; many close Sundays
- Markets: Marche d'Aligre (12th) for fresh produce and cheese on weekday mornings

TRANSPORT TO/FROM AIRPORT
- CDG to city center: RER B train (~45 min, ¥80) — most convenient
- Taxi from CDG: fixed fare ~¥320 to central Paris
- Uber: available, typically ¥250-300

BUDGET ESTIMATE (7 nights)
- Meals: ~¥200/day = ¥1,400 total
- Metro/transport: ~¥300 (weekly Navigo pass)
- Activities/entrance fees: ~¥500
- Estimated spending money: ¥2,200
